criteria.rationale: Verified the process marker and pidfd checks; the unresolved assumption is that a markerless reservation older than ten minutes has no live owner, which the code does not prove. L1/L2 are stated residual risks, but the age inference exceeds D2.
The publish-exclusive claim prevents simultaneous releases, but the claim and run/receipt sequence has unrecoverable interrupted states.
The attempt receipt and ordinary failed-run record retain the existing ledger shape; the CLI addition is scoped to stalled attempts without a latest run.
Unreadable reservation and receipt errors are suppressed by orphan discovery instead of being returned as losses.
The component integration surface still reaches the delegation lifecycle, and the focused CLI/pose tests pass.
delegate ls can omit a blocked unreadable markerless reservation without a diagnostic.
I examined the unchanged receipt schema and the released record fields; older readers see a normal failed run and no schema migration is introduced.
The release does not recover if interrupted between its durable claim, run record, and receipt.

D1's checkout marker and pidfd pin address escaped sessions and PID reuse; D2's release design addresses abandoned reservations, but the markerless age rule does not establish the dead-owner condition. The sealed structural assessment reports no deltas.
The manual says cancellation releases only after the owner is proven gone, while the markerless path releases by age without an owner proof.
After an interrupted release, the error names an in-progress/interrupted claim but gives no recovery action and subsequent cancellation remains blocked.
R5/R6 cover an interrupted dispatch, but the release transaction can itself leave a permanent incomplete attempt.
The changes are limited to the planned reaping, abandonment recovery, brief, tests, CLI and documentation surfaces.
An old live markerless dispatch can be misclassified as abandoned, release its reservation and overlap a subsequent dispatch.

The ten-minute age threshold is small but does not satisfy D2's proof of owner death. A safe alternative must identify the owner or leave a markerless attempt blocked with an actionable recovery path until absence is established.

findings.action: The exclusive .release claim has no recovery protocol. If cancellation is interrupted after publishing it, future cancel attempts are refused as already in progress/interrupted and the incomplete reservation remains blocking; interruption after the run write can also leave no receipt.

A markerless reservation is released based on age alone, without proving its dispatch owner is dead. An earlier engine paused after reserving can still be live after ten minutes; discarded marker/run loss reports also make absence unproven, allowing a live attempt to be released and overlap a later dispatch.

orphanReservations silently skips unreadable or invalid reservations and unreadable receipt paths. delegate ls then omits a blocked attempt without adding a loss diagnostic, while later admission can still refuse it.
